To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the channel gain, averaged over short time intervals, is log-normally and Rayleigh-distributed, (2) the channel gain autocorrelation function is exponentially decaying with the correlation time being inversely proportional to the signal bandwidth, (3) the short-term path gain is Ricean with Bessel-type correlation, (4) the large-scale transmission gain is exponentially distributed with an exponentially decays autocorrelation function.
the small-scale fading of the underwater acoustic channel is Rayleigh distributed, while the large-scale fading is log-normally (or log-Rayleigh) distributed.

the large-scale transmission losses are log-normally-distributed random variables whose autocorrelation decays exponentially with time, while the small-scale path coefficients are complex Gaussian random variables whose autocovariance is Bessel-type.
